title: Claude Fable 5.1’s Cache Lane Is 75% Cheaper. The Task Meter Can Still Run 20% Hot

items.claim: Fable 5.1 went live in Claude Code and the Claude Platform on September 1, alongside Mythos 5.1.
items.note: ClaudeDevs confirms availability in Claude Code and the Claude Platform; Anthropic confirms the joint launch, and the evidence package dates the release to September 1.

items.claim: Anthropic positions the models for coding, knowledge work, research, and long-running agentic work.
items.note: The official excerpt supports coding, knowledge work, and research; Anthropic-linked posts support long-running agentic work.

items.claim: Fable 5.1 retains Fable 5 pricing while API cache reads are 75% cheaper.
items.note: The source states both terms directly.

items.claim: TestingCatalog reported the same pricing terms and extra usage credits.
items.note: The excerpt says the model is priced the same as Fable 5, has 75% cheaper API cache reads, and requires extra usage credits.

items.claim: Anthropic estimates typical workloads can become roughly 25% cheaper.
items.note: No supplied evidence states the 25% typical-workload estimate. The package supports only savings of up to 45%.

items.claim: Savings can reach 45% for long agentic runs involving many tool calls.
items.note: The Decoder excerpt explicitly ties savings of up to 45% to long autonomous runs with many tool calls; The Verge title corroborates the upper figure.

items.claim: Artificial Analysis reported that Fable 5.1 topped its Intelligence Index but cost 20% more per task than Fable 5.
items.note: Both the ranking and 20% per-task cost increase appear directly in the excerpt.

items.claim: Artificial Analysis supported Anthropic's pre-release evaluation, so its result is not fully independent.
items.note: The relationship is stated directly; describing the resulting independence limitation is a clearly identified inference.

items.claim: The evidence does not disclose task-level token totals, cache-hit ratios, or effort settings needed to reconcile the cost results.
items.note: None of those details appears in the evidence package, so the article's absence statement is accurate.

items.claim: Cheaper cache reads and a higher total task cost can coexist if the model performs or processes more work.
items.note: This is explicitly framed as a possible reconciliation, not asserted as a measured cause.

items.claim: “It gets a lot further into a long task before it needs your input,” ClaudeDevs said.
items.note: The quoted clause matches the source verbatim. The original sentence continues with additional claims, but the omitted material does not change this complete clause's meaning.

items.claim: One circulating complaint described a 30-minute session consuming 20% of a weekly allowance.
items.note: The apparent source failed to fetch and contains no excerpt, so neither the 30-minute duration nor the 20% figure can be verified. The separate statement that the account could not be independently reviewed is accurate.

items.claim: Boris Cherny is an Anthropic staffer.
items.note: The package provides his name, account, and comments but no evidence of his employment or role at Anthropic. Consequently, the phrase 'inside Anthropic' is also unsupported here.

items.claim: Boris Cherny praised Fable 5.1 for difficult long-running agentic work and said he had been using it broadly.
items.note: His post calls it the best model for the hardest long-running agentic work and says he had been using it for everything.
The result appears directly in the source title and excerpt.

items.claim: Agentic coding improved by more than 30%.
items.note: The Decoder excerpt reports an improvement of over 30%.

items.claim: Precise assumptions behind the 25%, 45%, and 20% figures remain undisclosed in the evidence package.
items.note: The package provides headline percentages but no underlying workload assumptions or reconciliation data. This absence statement does not independently validate the unsupported 25% figure.

claim_check.reason: Most event claims, numerical results, quotations, source-level labels, and conditional inferences are supported or properly qualified. The article is nevertheless unsupported overall because the evidence package does not contain the claimed 25% typical-workload estimate, does not substantiate Boris Cherny's Anthropic role, and cannot verify the failed-source complaint's 30-minute and 20% details. No claim that 'both companies confirmed' appears in the article.

evidence_caveats: AA +20%/task 为单一来源且自曝参与官方预发布评测；每任务 token、effort、缓存命中假设均未公开，无独立复测
叙事所指的隐藏变量——每任务 token 基数——双方均未公布，无法直接核验；决策规则已以「等官方口径」兜底
官方完整价格表未抓全（platform.claude.com release notes 正文未获取）；缓存读取绝对价 0.25/M 仅机器之心等二手渠道；缓存写入价是否同步降 Unknown
订阅「额外 usage credits」倍率与触发条件未披露（TestingCatalog 提及），无法并入测算
自测框架依赖 Claude Code 用量导出能力，仅社区用户帖间接佐证，无官方文档
frxiaobei 帖 404、部分知乎页面二次打开 403/仅 found：社区侧证未抓全，但不承载核心价格论点
Boris Cherny 职务与雇佣关系未披露，只能按个人口吻引用（当前处理合规，持续注意）
seo_title: Claude Fable 5.1: Cheaper Cache, Costlier Tasks
seo_summary: Cache reads cost 75% less, yet one benchmark found 20% higher task costs. Measure cost per successful outcome before switching.
